about.title: Mount Shasta Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Mount Shasta's economy runs on tourism, forestry, and services that keep travelers moving along Interstate 5, and workers in warehouses, hospitality, retail, and roadside operations all face daily injury risk. When California's workers' compensation system applies, it's usually your only path against your employer, no matter who caused the accident. But that exclusivity doesn't extend to outside parties: a subcontractor on a job site, a negligent driver near N Mt Shasta Boulevard, a property owner, or the maker of faulty equipment can still be held liable in a separate injury claim. Siskiyou County's small-town feel doesn't mean these situations are simple; overlapping comp and third-party rules trip up a lot of injured workers. LawProactive doesn't practice law, but we can connect you at no cost with an independent attorney who reviews your situation and explains what avenues might be open to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Independent Attorney First

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: California treats workers' comp as the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party, like a contractor or equipment manufacturer, can still be pursued separately.

items.title: Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report an injury to your employer, and a third-party claim carries its own 2-year filing deadline, so waiting can cost you options.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from punishing you for reporting a workplace injury, and an attorney can help you understand your protections if you feel pressured.

items.question: I was hurt while driving for work near I-5 in Mount Shasta. Is that just a workers' comp case?
items.answer: It might involve both. Workers' comp usually covers your medical costs and lost wages regardless of fault, but if another driver caused the crash, a separate third-party claim against that driver may also be possible. An independent attorney can look at the details and explain how the two claims interact.

items.question: What if my employer says I can't file because I waited too long?
items.answer: California generally requires reporting a workplace injury within 30 days, so delays can complicate things, but every situation has its own facts. It's worth getting a free case review rather than assuming your options are closed.

items.question: Can I still get help if I'm not sure whether workers' comp or a lawsuit fits my situation?
items.answer: Yes, that's exactly the kind of question an independent attorney sorts out. LawProactive doesn't decide legal strategy, but we can connect you with someone who reviews the facts of your Mount Shasta workplace injury and points you toward the right process, at no cost to you.
